answer: A reputation system can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before transacting, with the stake rising as the delta between its claimed history and verified work widens. New identities start with a thin, shale-like trust layer: they may only take small jobs until peers attest their deliveries. Each successful attestation adds a transparent, crystal-clear record to a shared ledger, so a fake identity must pay real stake and do real work for every persona it spawns, making large-scale fakery more expensive than honest participation.
